MUQATIL:10:89-91/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:89-91/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:89-91/r3.claim: Gabriel put a handful of sea gravel into Pharaoh's mouth; Muqatil glosses “now” as faith at death and “corruptors” as disobedient people.

TAB-FULL:v12p278#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p278#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p278#2/r1.claim: God rebukes Pharaoh for professing submission only as punishment and death arrive, after earlier disobedience and corruption by turning people from God's path; Pharaoh should have repented while time remained.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's finger emerged from the sea as he declared belief; Gabriel feared mercy might reach him and struck him with a wing, reproaching his late repentance.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says Pharaoh saw God's power and humiliation, then professed belief in Israel's God and submission.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r3.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh's cry came too late; had it occurred during ease, it could have counted.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1983/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says God sent Mika'il to reproach Pharaoh with the words, now, after you had disobeyed.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r1.claim: Nafi's transmitters vary in how they render آلآن: some ask it with one hamza, while Warsh lengthens the initial hamza, opens lām, and omits the second hamza by transferring its vowel.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r2.speaker: باقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r2.claim: The other readers retain the hamza after lām and keep lām quiescent; reports from Qalun also describe a single hamza followed by lengthening.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p296/r3.claim: When the definite article precedes an initial hamza that is lightened, Arabic may transfer its vowel to lām and keep hamzat al-waṣl, or delete hamzat al-waṣl; both pronunciations have evidence.

THALABI:v5p146/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p146/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p146/r1.claim: Moses had announced that God might destroy the enemy and install Israel in the land, then test how they acted; he also declared that his Lord was with him and would guide him.

THALABI:v5p146/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p146/r5.speaker: جبريل
THALABI:v5p146/r5.claim: As Pharaoh drowned and professed belief in Israel’s God, Gabriel put sea mud into his mouth, and the Quran rebuked his late faith.

THALABI:v5p146/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p146/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v5p146/r6.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says God had ordered Moses and Aaron to speak gently to Pharaoh, whose eventual remembrance and fear came too late to help.

THALABI:v5p146/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p146/r7.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p146/r7.claim: Kaʿb relates that after the Nile stopped, Pharaoh privately prostrated and pleaded for water; Gabriel came as a petitioner asking how a servant’s betrayal should be punished, and Pharaoh wrote that he should drown.

THALABI:v5p147/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p147/r8.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p147/r8.claim: The Prophet reports Gabriel hated Iblis and Pharaoh most among jinn and humans; Gabriel says he put mud in Pharaoh’s mouth lest mercy reach him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r3.claim: With open hamza, the verb 'believe' ordinarily takes a preposition, which is omitted here so the anna-clause becomes its object or genitive; with kasra, an unspoken 'I said' is understood, and this reading highlights that the confession expresses faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and all exegetes say Pharaoh's declaration was rejected because he professed faith only as punishment arrived; only Jonah's people were accepted at that stage, before death was visibly present.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r5.claim: The exegetes say the angels confronted Pharaoh with 'Now?'—he had delayed repentance, chosen temporary life, and sought it only when the gate closed; they identify Gabriel as the speaker.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r6.claim: Al-āna is attached to an omitted predicate supplied by context, such as 'now you believe', 'believe', or 'repent'.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r7.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p301/r7.claim: The author of al-Naẓm argues a drowning man could scarcely utter the full confession; the verse reports the certainty and remorse God knew in Pharaoh's heart as speech, like inward speech represented in 58:8 and 76:9.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r4.claim: Pharaoh's declaration came only after he saw and faced death, when faith or repentance could no longer help him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:89-92/r5.claim: “Now?” rebukes Pharaoh for believing or repenting only at the moment of death, after prior disobedience.

JISHUMI:v5p3420#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3420#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3420#2/r9.claim: The governing word before آلآن is omitted and understood as آلآن آمنت; آلآن is a built deictic for the present, and its lām marks definiteness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p148/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p148/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p148/r7.claim: When the Israelites doubted Pharaoh had died, the sea cast his short red body ashore, fulfilling the following verse about preserving his body.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p348#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p348#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p348#3/r4.claim: Pharaoh repeated one meaning in three formulations in hope of acceptance, but his confession was rejected because he spoke after choice and moral responsibility had ended.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r1.claim: ‘Now?’ questions faith at the moment of desperation, when drowning has overtaken him and he has lost hope; views differ whether he spoke as he choked, just before drowning, or after internally drowning.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r2.claim: The story that Gabriel stuffed sea mud into Pharaoh's mouth is a blasphemous fabrication, not an obstacle to heartfelt faith; hating an unbeliever's faith itself amounts to disbelief.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r3.claim: The two objections to the mud story are that faith is valid in the heart even for a mute person, and that one who prefers an unbeliever to remain disbelieving is himself an unbeliever.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r4.claim: Mufsidin means those who are astray and lead others away from faith.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p349/r5.claim: A report says Gabriel asked Pharaoh for a ruling about a servant raised in his master's wealth who denied his benefactor and claimed mastery; Pharaoh wrote that such a rebel should drown, and Gabriel showed him the ruling as he drowned.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r2.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r2.claim: When the definite article precedes a word beginning with hamza that is softened, one may delete the hamza and move its vowel to lām, or delete the connecting hamza as well; Sibawayh and Abu al-Hasan attest these forms, with a poem cited as evidence.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r3.speaker: نافع عن ورش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r3.claim: Warsh from Nafi reads الآن with a prolonged hamza and open lām; other readers prolong the first hamza, leave lām unvocalized, and pronounce the second hamza, while additional readings shorten or soften the hamzas.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r4.claim: The softened-hamza readings follow Abu Ali's analysis; the wording reproaches Pharaoh and announces punishment, and may be an actual message delivered by an angel or a portrayal of his state and humiliation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p141/r5.claim: This verse explicitly shows that repentance after witnessing death is not accepted.

TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r6.claim: The rebuke means that belief is useless now, under compulsion, when it would have helped before; Pharaoh had corrupted the land through killing believers, claiming divinity, and other unbelief.

TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r7.claim: The rebuke is attributed either to Gabriel or to God speaking in humiliation and reproach; the event was a miracle for Moses.

TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r8.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:10:90-92#2/r8.claim: Al-Sadiq relates that Gabriel told Muhammad he had stuffed mud into Pharaoh's mouth after the profession of faith, fearing that mercy might reach Pharaoh and God might punish Gabriel; he later learned God approved the act.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r1.claim: “Now?” rebukes Pharaoh for trying to repent after wasting the proper time; he was corrupt by calling people to worship other than God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r2.claim: Gabriel addressed Pharaoh; a hadith says Gabriel stuffed clay into Pharaoh's mouth, fearing God might forgive him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r3.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p60/r3.claim: Remember God in ease and He will remember you in hardship; Jonah remembered God and was rescued, while Pharaoh had forgotten God and only professed faith while drowning.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r1.claim: One proposed explanation is that Pharaoh's confession was invalid because he believed in a bodily deity who indwells creatures, an error associated here with Israelite calf worship.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that valid faith required both God's oneness and Moses' prophethood; Pharaoh professed oneness without professing the messenger.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf relates a story in which Gabriel asked Pharaoh to rule on an ungrateful servant who claimed lordship; Pharaoh prescribed drowning, and Gabriel presented the judgment to him as he drowned.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r4.claim: Reports identify the speaker of the rebuke “now?” as Gabriel, contrasting Pharaoh's claim to be Muslim with his former conduct.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r5.claim: Others identify God as the speaker because the following declaration that Pharaoh's body will be saved for a sign is divine speech.

RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p124#2/r6.claim: An objection notes that the verse seems to say past rebellion explains why repentance was not accepted, though that fact alone does not rule out acceptance; the excerpt ends before the reply.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r1.claim: One view attributes the words to God speaking to Pharaoh.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r2.claim: Alternative attributions make Gabriel, Michael, or another angel the speaker addressing Pharaoh.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r3.claim: Another view says Pharaoh himself thought the words inwardly rather than speaking them aloud; Qurtubi compares God’s praise of an inward intention elsewhere.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:91/r4.claim: The comparison shows that genuine speech can be speech of the heart, since God describes the feeding intention of the righteous without requiring spoken wording.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:91-92/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:91-92/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:91-92/r1.claim: Pharaoh is asked whether he believes only now, after he has lost choice and hope, despite disobeying throughout his life and leading others astray.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r1.claim: The rebuke asks whether Pharaoh believes now, at the moment of compulsion when drowning has overtaken him and he despairs; the interrogative now is governed by 'do you believe?'

NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r2.claim: Earlier disobedience made Pharaoh one of those who led others astray from faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p140#4/r3.claim: Gabriel brought Pharaoh a legal question about a servant raised in his master's wealth who denied the master's favor and claimed lordship; al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab wrote that such a rebel deserved drowning, and Gabriel showed Pharaoh the ruling as he choked.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r5.claim: The rebuke beginning آلآن is apparently God's speech through an angel, identified variously as Gabriel, Michael, or another; another view makes it Pharaoh's own inner speech.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p102/r6.claim: Treating فاليوم ننجيك as a question of threat is unlikely because it requires an omitted interrogative hamza and makes the purpose clause about becoming a sign incoherent.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r1.claim: God's reply means Pharaoh professes faith only now, after prior disobedience; he had corrupted the earth by misleading people.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r2.claim: Pharaoh's exact words at death are among hidden matters God disclosed to His Messenger.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying Gabriel took mud from the sea and put it in Pharaoh's mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him; al-Tirmidhi grades this route hasan.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p292/r4.claim: A second Ibn ʿAbbas route has al-Tirmidhi grading the report hasan gharib sahih; a Jarir route raises it through one of two narrators, while Ibn Kathir leaves that variation uncertain.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir also transmits the Abu Khalid report from Ibn ʿAbbas as mawquf rather than attributing it to the Prophet.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying Gabriel gagged Pharaoh with sea mud lest God's mercy reach him; the narrator Kathir ibn Zadhan is unknown to Ibn Maʿin, Abu Zurʿa, and Abu Hatim, though the rest are reliable.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p293/r3.claim: The report is also sent as a mursal narration from Qatada, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and Maymun ibn Mihran; it was preached by al-Dahhak ibn Qays, and Ibn Kathir says God knows best.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r5.claim: Now? rebukes a reply made when faith in the unseen can no longer benefit him; Pharaoh had disobeyed throughout the prior call and was deeply corrupt.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r6.claim: The rebuke may be spoken by God, Gabriel, the Angel of Death, or another of the angelic hosts.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p477/r8.claim: He rejects claims that Pharaoh's profession here proves his faith: the consensus of religious communities calls him among the most unbelieving, and the claim would trivialize sin.

DURR-FULL:v4p386/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r1.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r1.claim: In the narrative, Gabriel says the sea cast Pharaoh's naked body ashore as a sign for those who denied his drowning; this was a sign, not a safe deliverance.

DURR-FULL:v4p386/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that Gabriel stuffed sea mud into Pharaoh's mouth as he drowned, fearing that divine mercy might reach him; al-Tirmidhi grades one version hasan.

DURR-FULL:v4p386/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r3.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report repeats that Gabriel put mud in Pharaoh's mouth for fear of mercy; the cited Tirmidhi version is graded sound.

DURR-FULL:v4p386/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r4.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r4.claim: Gabriel says he put mud in Pharaoh's mouth to prevent him prolonging his plea, knowing the breadth of God's mercy.

DURR-FULL:v4p386/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r5.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p386/r5.claim: Gabriel says he hated Pharaoh and stuffed his mouth with mire while holding him down, fearing mercy would reach him.

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r1.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r1.claim: Gabriel says he pressed Pharaoh down and put mire into his mouth, fearing God would forgive him.

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.claim: Gabriel recounts that Pharaoh had claimed divinity, then stuffed his mouth when drowning threatened, fearing he would receive mercy.

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Gabriel wore a black turban on the day Pharaoh drowned.

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r4.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying Gabriel feared Pharaoh might sincerely utter monotheism and be saved, so he put mud in his mouth; God ordered Michael to rebuke Gabriel.

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says God sent Michael to taunt Pharaoh with the rebuke, “Now, after you disobeyed before.”

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r6.claim: Abu Bakr says he was told Pharaoh had broken or missing front teeth.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r1.claim: The interrogative آلآن rebukes Pharaoh for professing faith only after despairing of life; an omitted verb is estimated after the adverb to direct the reproach at the delay.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r2.claim: The rebuke is attributed variously to God, Gabriel, or Michael.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r3.claim: A report from Abū Umāma via Abū al-Shaykh says Gabriel hated Pharaoh, feared he might utter the confession and escape, put mud into his mouth, and that God became angrier than Gabriel.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the report fabrications against God and the angels: a blocked mouth cannot prevent inward faith, and hating a disbeliever's faith would itself be unbelief; Ibn al-Munīr endorses his objection.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#2/r5.claim: A report transmitted by several collectors and authenticated by al-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim has Gabriel say that he put sea mud into Pharaoh's mouth lest mercy reach him.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r1.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r1.claim: Irshād construes mercy as worldly rescue, which need not entail valid faith, as in the case of Jonah's people; Gabriel merely closed off a remote possibility. Al-Ālūsī finds this reading unlikely.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r2.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says Gabriel covered Pharaoh with one hand and put mud in his mouth fearing God's mercy might reach him and God forgive him; al-Ālūsī says this denotes forgiveness, not earthly rescue.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r3.claim: Another verifier explains Gabriel's act as anger and fear that repeated confession might, by extraordinary mercy, be accepted; he says approving one's own unbelief is unbelief, while disapproving another's is not necessarily so.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī says sound transmitted reports should be accepted even when reason cannot explain them, with the limitation assigned to the reader.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī counters that if a report contradicts clear reason or attributes an impossible defect to an infallible angel and admits no sound interpretation, doubt should fall on its transmitter rather than reason.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p182#3/r6.claim: The phrase وقد عصيت قبل is a circumstantial clause intensifying the rebuke: Pharaoh delayed faith without excuse, while his corruption also harmed others through oppression and blocking Israel's way.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r1.claim: The words are God's reply to Pharaoh's profession of faith, understood as a request to escape drowning after acknowledging God's lordship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r2.claim: God speaks through the angel assigned to punish Pharaoh to extinguish his hope of salvation in this life and the next.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r3.claim: Pharaoh had recognized Moses' claims and hoped that confessing divine unity would secure rescue; the following verse confirms that context.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r4.claim: The question “Now?” is a rebuke; an omitted verb is “now you believe,” with the time placed first because it is the focus of denial.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r5.claim: The rebuke means faith at the moment of death cannot save its bearer in this world or the next.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r6.claim: The time word “now” denotes the present, as in the earlier usage in al-Anfal.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p277#2/r7.claim: The circumstantial clause intensifies the rebuke: Pharaoh had disobeyed, corrupted religion, and spread earthly oppression and deception by magic.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p278/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p278/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p278/r1.claim: “You were among the corrupters” is more emphatic than simply calling him a corrupter; greater wrongdoing brings more severe punishment.

TABATABAI:10:91-92/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:91-92/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:91-92/r1.claim: Al-an now is lengthened from two hamzas; Pharaoh is rebuked for professing faith only when punishment and death surround him, after a life of disobedience and corruption.

TABATABAI:10:91-92/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:91-92/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:91-92/r2.claim: This is the moment Moses and Aaron had asked God to bring about: Pharaoh would be barred from believing until punishment came, when faith and repentance could no longer help.

ASAD-NOTES:10:91#n111/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:91#n111/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:91#n111/r1.claim: The rebuke asks whether Pharaoh is repenting only at the point when repentance is too late.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Historical accounts from Noah through Moses parallel the Prophet’s and companions’ opposition; steadfastness and trust in God lead to success for them and defeat for their opponents.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Pharaoh’s profession of faith while drowning depicts helplessness: tyrants acknowledge the truth when seized, but this late acknowledgment bears no fruit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The rebuke asking whether Pharaoh believes only now may describe his state rather than words actually spoken.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r1.claim: Israel left Egypt at God’s command; the sea split, Israel crossed with divine aid, and Pharaoh and his followers drowned.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r2.speaker: the majority of Islamic scholars
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:90/r2.claim: Although scholars debated whether Pharaoh’s last-minute words constituted faith, most concluded his faith was invalid, considering the verse’s wording and other evidence.

STUDYQURAN:10:90/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:90/r1.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:10:90/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s rhetorical rebuke means that repentance when no alternative remains is too late and will not be accepted.

STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r17.claim: The closing accounts of Noah and Moses contrast with Jonah's people, who heed their prophet's warning and avert punishment, showing people can still accept truth and benefit by escaping punishment.
